summary: Berlin office: intermittent captive portal + WireGuard split-tunnel causing internal DNS failures
description:
Issue summary:
Employee (BER-017) reports inability to reach internal services (git.redwood, console.redwood-inference) when on office Wi‑Fi and connected to corporate WireGuard VPN. Intermittent behavior: sometimes services work after reconnect but then fail again. Impact: blocked developer, SSO pages failing, critical deploy delayed.

Impact:
- Single developer impacted initially, potential for more if root cause is AP or DNS policy.
- Affects access to internal git and console (portals behind internal DNS).

Environment:
- Location: Berlin HQ (floor 3).
- Client: Windows 11 laptop (Dell XPS), VPN client: company WireGuard profile (wg0), Wi‑Fi: Meraki MR access points (SSID: Redwood-Staff).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Join SSID Redwood-Staff and authenticate via 802.1X (OK).
2) Establish WireGuard tunnel (wg-quick up redwood-wg).
3) Attempt to resolve internal hostnames (git.internal, console.internal).
4) Observe failures intermittently; traceroute shows packets leaving client to public DNS instead of corporate DNS.

Observed behavior / Logs:
- nslookup git.internal -> Server: 1.1.1.1
  Address: 1.1.1.1#53
  ** server can't find git.internal: NXDOMAIN
- ping console.internal -> Destination host unreachable (no route to 10.48.10.5)
- wg show: interface up, peers present, allowed-ips = 10.48.0.0/16, 10.0.0.0/8, but resolv.conf shows 1.1.1.1
- Browser developer reported DoH (DNS over HTTPS) enabled in Firefox which points to cloudflare-dns.com

Initial hypothesis:
- Split-tunnel policy should push corporate DNS (10.0.0.53) to the client but DoH in the browser and a cached system DNS configuration are causing name resolution to bypass the WireGuard-supplied resolver. Additionally, a recent firmware push to a subset of MR APs enabled client isolation/captive-portal fallback that intermittently breaks DHCP/DNS update during fast roaming.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Connect to Redwood-Staff SSID and authenticate 2) Start WireGuard profile redwood-wg 3) Try to resolve git.internal and open console.internal 4) Note DNS server and traceroute outputs
investigation_notes:
- Confirmed user was on MR-AP MR33, firmware 28.6.1; AP had recent config change (rollout-berlin-2026-03-02).
- Reproduced on second laptop: enabling DoH in Firefox caused internal names to fail even with wg0 present.
- Captive portal: observed DHCP lease refresh failed during AP fast-roam; client sometimes dropped system DNS to AP-supplied DNS until reconnect.
- WireGuard config contains PostUp scripts intended to update resolv.conf but was being overwritten by NetworkManager on Windows when DHCP events fired.
- No evidence of central WireGuard server rejecting DNS push; server-side logs show successful handshake and routes assigned.
hypothesis: Primary cause is a race between AP DHCP events (client roaming) and WireGuard's DNS push/update; DoH in-browser masks the system resolver changes leading client to query public resolvers. Secondary contributor: AP client isolation feature triggers captive portal behavior during the roam, briefly removing local DNS and routes.
actions_taken: Scoped incident to BER floor 3 and disabled recent AP change (client-isolation) on MR33 cluster as quick mitigation
Advised user to temporarily disable DoH in browser and flush DNS cache (ipconfig /flushdns)
Applied Windows local workaround: run wg-quick down/up + netsh interface ip set dns to force corporate DNS 10.0.0.53
SRE verified WireGuard server logs and confirmed allowed-ips and DNS push succeeded
Opened ticket with Meraki support referencing rollout-berlin-2026-03-02 for firmware behavior
resolution:
Workaround provided: disable browser DoH and re-establish wg0; AP change rolled back for affected cluster. Root fix pending: update Windows WireGuard wrapper to force system resolver update post-tunnel-up and patch Meraki roaming config. Owners: Networking team (rollout fix) and SRE (VPN client update). Targeted change window scheduled for 2026-03-18.

Follow-up items:
- Deploy WireGuard client update (force resolv.conf update on tunnel up) - owner: SRE - ETA 2026-03-18
- Audit MR AP clusters for similar config drift - owner: NetEng - ETA 2026-03-20
- Add DoH detection and UX warning in internal onboarding docs - owner: IT Docs - ETA 2026-04-01
comments: 2026-03-12 - Maya Patel (Support): User reported issue at 09:22 CET. Confirmed intermittent failures. Escalated to SRE.
2026-03-12 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Performed live debug with user at 10:05 CET. Reproduced DNS going to 1.1.1.1 despite wg0 up. Captured wireguard and system logs.
2026-03-12 - Jana Müller (NetEng): Rolled back MR33 client-isolation change for BER cluster at 11:30 CET. Asked Meraki to investigate roaming DHCP behavior.
2026-03-13 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Confirmed workaround (disable DoH + wg restart) resolves immediate symptoms. Scheduling client update to enforce DNS push on tunnel up.
2026-03-13 - IT Ops (note): Workaround communicated to BER floor via Slack #berlin-office. Monitoring for recurrence.
